title: What the satellites recorded
description: What satellites recorded in northern Arakan in autumn 2017: the 1,862 destroyed zones the UN mapped, set against 1,023 Rohingya villages by name.
summary: In the autumn of 2017, satellites passing over northern Arakan photographed Rohingya villages, and analysts at the United Nations mapped where buildings had been destroyed. This is what that record shows for the villages in this archive, and what it cannot show.

steps.html:
The archive

{{n}} villages, each with a name

Every dot is a Rohingya village in one of four townships of Arakan, the land Myanmar calls Rakhine State: Maungdaw, Buthidaung, Rathedaung and Sittwe.

FARA keeps each village's name as its people say it, beside its official name and its name in Burmese. Fará is the Rohingya word for village.

August 2017

The villages emptied

From late August 2017, more than 750,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh, according to the UN refugee agency. Most came from the three northern townships on this map.

What happened to the places they left was recorded from above.

steps.html:
The survey

{{n_zones}}destroyed zones
mapped by UNOSAT

UNOSAT studied satellite images of Maungdaw, Buthidaung and Rathedaung taken between 31 August and 11 October 2017, and outlined every zone where it found buildings destroyed.

It mapped {{n_zones}} zones, about {{zone_ha}} hectares in all. This is Maungdaw township, where most of them lie.

Against the names

{{n_destroyed}}villages in this archive
with destroyed buildings

Set against the villages FARA has on record, {{n_destroyed}} had destroyed buildings mapped at their recorded position. Another {{n_nearby}} had a destroyed zone within 500 metres.

What it cannot show

“None detected” is not “still standing”

At {{n_none}} villages UNOSAT marked no destroyed zone within 500 metres. That is not proof those villages stand.

The imagery ends on 11 October 2017. Parts of the area were under cloud. Destruction went on after that date, and UNOSAT did not check its findings on the ground.

Sittwe township, with {{sittwe_all}} villages in this archive, lay outside the survey altogether.

The names remain

Every village had a name

A village is more than its buildings. Its name carries the memory of the people who lived there, and a name is the easiest thing to erase: by renaming a place, or by leaving it off the map.

FARA keeps the names. If you know one this archive is missing or has wrong, tell us.

method: How villages were matched: a village is counted as destroyed when a UNOSAT zone covers its recorded position or at least one hectare is marked destroyed within 300 metres of it, and as “nearby” when any zone lies within 500 metres. Matching is by position only and has not been reviewed village by village. The per-village results are in status_unosat_2017.csv.
